title: Gardyn's Black Friday Sale on the Home 4 and Studio 2 Ends Monday — What the 25% Off Price Doesn't Tell You
intro: Gardyn is running 25% off its Home 4 and Studio 2 indoor hydroponic systems from Thanksgiving Day through Cyber Monday, November 30 — Bob Vila's deal desk flagged it as the brand's best discount of the year, and Gardyn's own site and its Rakuten storefront confirm the same window and pricing. The Home 4 Classic drops to $674.25 from its regular $899, and the smaller Studio 2 Classic drops to $411.75 from $549. For apartment growers without a yard, a Gardyn is a real alternative to a windowsill full of individual pots — it's a self-contained vertical hydroponic column with its own lights and watering, not a grow light you have to build a setup around. But the sale price is only half the real cost of owning one, and that's the part worth working through before Monday's deadline, not after.

sections.heading: Home 4 vs. Studio 2 — which one actually fits your apartment
sections.body: The two models aren't just different price points, they're different footprints. The Home 4 holds 30 plants in roughly 2 square feet of floor space and is rated for up to 10 pounds of harvest a month — it's the one built for someone trying to replace a real chunk of their produce buying. The Studio 2, which Gardyn launched in October 2025 as a redesigned, easier-to-clean version of its original Studio, holds 16 plants in about 1.4 square feet and tops out around 5 pounds a month — closer to a serious herb-and-salad-greens setup than a full produce replacement. If your apartment's constraint is floor space rather than ambition, the Studio 2 at $411.75 is the one that actually fits next to a couch or in a kitchen corner; the Home 4 at $674.25 wants a dedicated spot the way a bookshelf would.

products.name: Gardyn Home 4 indoor hydroponic garden
products.blurb: Gardyn's larger column, 30 plant sites and up to 10 lbs/month of harvest in about 2 sq ft — the one that makes sense if you're trying to meaningfully cut produce spending rather than just keep fresh herbs on hand.
products.priceNote: Listed at $899 regularly; Gardyn's Black Friday sale through Nov. 30, 2026 brings the Classic version to $674.25 (25% off) per Bob Vila and Gardyn's own site.

products.name: Gardyn Studio 2 indoor hydroponic garden
products.blurb: The smaller, redesigned-in-2025 column — 16 plant sites, about 1.4 sq ft of footprint, up to 5 lbs/month — sized for a kitchen counter or a corner rather than a dedicated room.
products.priceNote: Listed at $549 regularly; the same Black Friday sale brings the Classic version to $411.75 (25% off).

sections.heading: The number that actually matters: the membership, not the hardware price
sections.body: Gardyn's site describes its membership as "highly recommended" rather than optional, and that framing is accurate — without it, the app reportedly drops back to basic water-level alerts and loses the monthly pod credits (10 for the Home 4, 5 for the Studio 2), the plant-care guidance, and features like vacation mode. Reported membership pricing isn't consistent across Gardyn's own pages and independent reviews: figures in the $19–$25/month range show up alongside an older listing near $35/month, and at least one Trustpilot reviewer reported a recent app change moving some previously-free reminders behind a $29/month tier. That spread matters because it changes the real first-year cost: a Home 4 at the sale price plus a year of membership runs anywhere from roughly $900 to over $1,000 depending on which membership tier you actually get billed, not the $674 the sale price alone suggests. Before buying, confirm the current membership price directly on mygardyn.com at checkout rather than from older marketing pages — and note that Gardyn's holiday price-match guarantee covers Home 4 and Studio 2 purchases made on its own site between Nov. 1 and Dec. 31, 2026, so buying now rather than waiting doesn't lock in a worse price if the discount deepens later this season.

products.name: Gardyn Home 4 membership plan
products.blurb: The subscription Gardyn bills as highly recommended rather than optional — it's what actually delivers the monthly pod credits and plant-care support the hardware is designed around, and it's the cost the sale price doesn't include.
products.priceNote: Reported pricing varies by source (roughly $19-$35/month) — confirm the current rate at checkout on mygardyn.com before buying on the hardware discount alone.

conclusion: If a self-contained hydroponic column is genuinely what your apartment needs — no windowsill, no grow-light shopping, no separate watering routine — this is a real discount on real hardware, confirmed across Gardyn's own site, Bob Vila, and Rakuten, and it closes with Cyber Monday on November 30. Just price the membership before you price the unit: the 25% off sticker price is the smaller number in what you'll actually spend this year, and that's the number worth nailing down before the sale window closes, not after the first bill arrives.
